unit.name: Agent architecture: memory, tools, resources, autonomy, and MCP
unit.description: Breaks down a travel-booking agent into prompts, context management, memory, tools, resources, autonomy levels, APIs, and Model Context Protocol.
unit.summary: A travel booking agent is used to explain core components: prompts, context management, memory, tools, and resources [ts=4020s]. Memory is split into working memory for frequently needed facts and archival memory for less frequently accessed facts, because retrieving memory on every model call can add latency [ts=4054s]. Tools include APIs such as flight search, hotel booking, car rental, weather, and payment, while resources are data sources such as CRM records that an agent may read through lookup tools [ts=4148s]. Autonomy ranges from hard-coded steps, to fixed tools with flexible steps, to systems that decide steps and create tools or code [ts=4216s]. The instructor then contrasts one-off API integrations with MCP, which places a protocol layer between the agent and endpoints to make tool/resource access more scalable through agent-to-agent communication [ts=4339s]. The Q&A also notes that MCP security and memory design remain active, unsolved engineering concerns [ts=4519s].

key_points.text: A travel agent can be decomposed into prompts, a context management system, memory, tools, and resources.
Working memory stores frequently needed user facts; archival memory stores less frequently accessed facts.
Tool APIs can include flight search, hotel booking, car rental, weather, and payment processing.
Resources are data stores an agent can read, such as a CRM used for lookup.
Least autonomous systems hard-code steps; semi-autonomous systems hard-code tools but not steps; more autonomous systems decide steps and may create tools.
MCP provides a middle layer so the agent can communicate with tools or data endpoints without hard-coding every API integration.
MCP may introduce security requirements depending on the sensitivity of exposed data and authentication boundaries.

kp_catalog.name: Agent memory, tools, and resources
kp_catalog.description: Core components of an agentic system, including prompt logic, memory layers, API tools, and readable data resources.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Memory/tools/resources are concrete agent components supporting the agentic-workflow concept.

kp_catalog.name: Agent autonomy levels
kp_catalog.description: A spectrum from hard-coded steps, to fixed tools with flexible planning, to more autonomous systems that choose steps and create tools or code.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The autonomy spectrum helps students reason about safety, control, and product design decisions in agent systems [ts=4216s].

kp_catalog.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
kp_catalog.description: A standardized interface layer that lets agents communicate with tools or data providers more efficiently than bespoke API-by-API integrations.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: MCP is introduced as an emerging practical standard for connecting agents to tools and resources but the instructor notes security and maturity concerns [ts=4339s].
